title: R$^3$L: Reasoning 3D Layouts from Relative Spatial Relations
claim: Prior methods reason over long coupled relation chains that accumulate errors and drift; decomposing into short sub-chains keeps outputs consistent.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels split by dashed line, top-to-bottom flow, red vs green
description: The figure is split into a left panel for previous methods and a right panel for the proposed method, separated by a vertical dashed gray line. A dashed box at the top holds a natural-language instruction about a sofa, TV stand, coffee table and lounge chairs, with the spatial relations in green italics. Down the left side, arrows run through three labeled stages: Instructions, Relations, Scenes. The left panel shows one connected relation graph labeled 'Coupled Chain' in red. The right panel shows the same graph split into two smaller graphs, labeled 'Decomposed Chains' in green. Below the graphs are top-down furniture layouts. On the left, red dashed outlines mark chairs overlapping the sofa and a misplaced table, captioned 'Drifted Layouts'. On the right, the objects are cleanly arranged, captioned 'Consistent Layouts'. Text below names semantic drift and metric drift, and a legend maps node letters to furniture icons. Red versus green gives the contrast at a glance.
caption: Previous methods (left) reason over coupled relation chains, where repeated reference-frame transformations accumulate errors in inferred relations and lead to drifted layouts. In contrast, \nickname (right) decomposes long coupled chains into shorter sub-chains to reduce reference-frame transformations and error accumulation, producing feasible and consistent layouts.
abstract: Relative spatial relations provide a compact representation of spatial structure and are fundamental to relative spatial reasoning in 3D layout generation. Recent works leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to infer such relations, but the inferred relations are often unreliable and are typically handled with post-hoc heuristics. In this paper, we propose R$^3$L, a general framework that improves the reliability and consistency of relative spatial reasoning for 3D layout generation. Our key motivation is that multi-hop reasoning requires repeated reference-frame transformations, which accumulate errors in inferred relations and lead to semantic and metric drift. To mitigate this, we propose invariant spatial decomposition to break coupled relation chains, and consistent spatial imagination to promote self-consistency through an imagine-and-revise loop. We further introduce supportive spatial optimization to ease pose optimization via global-to-local coordinate re-parameterization. Extensive experiments across diverse scene types and instructions demonstrate that R$^3$L produces more physically feasible and semantically consistent layouts. Notably, our analysis shows that resolving frame-induced inconsistencies is crucial for reliable multi-hop relative spatial reasoning. The code is available at https://github.com/Neal2020GitHub/R3L.
